THE IDEA

Why we made First Glance.

Everything on this page comes from the same small moment: a child, a grown-up and a picture, saying a word together. Before classes and worksheets and learning paths, there is this — a first glance at the world, one labelled picture at a time.

We made these sheets because the very first words deserve very clear pictures. Every sheet holds a little family of things that belong together — pets, fruit, feelings, shapes — drawn big and bold with the word right underneath. No app, no login, no sound needed: open a sheet and start pointing.

The two groups follow how vocabulary really grows. Ages 2–3 names the everyday world a toddler can see and touch. Ages 4–5 stretches into ideas — seasons, jobs, positions, safety — the sheets that turn naming into asking and answering. Both meet your child wherever they are: there is no wrong sheet to start with.

Keep it short and keep it warm. One or two sheets, a few minutes, plenty of chat. That is the whole method — and it is the one that works.

How to use the sheets.

01

Point and name

Tap a sheet, then point at each picture and say the word clearly. Let your child point and say it back — echoing is learning.

02

Ask little questions

“Where is the cat?” “Which one do we eat?” Questions turn naming into thinking, and every answer earns a reply.

03

Bring it to life

Meet a dog after the pets sheet, stir the pot after the kitchen sheet. Words stick when the real thing shows up.

04

Print and keep

Every sheet opens full size — print it for the kitchen wall, the car ride or the waiting room. Repetition is the point.
